title: Reduce CI Docker layer churn, add cache observability, and refresh lint/toolchain
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: CI build times and image churn have regressed over the past 18 months due to incremental toolchain changes, fragmented Docker bases, and no unified visibility into cache hit rates. This work reduces layer churn, ships cache observability, and consolidates lint/toolchain upgrades to cut developer feedback loops and CI costs.

Scope: (1) Introduce stable minimal base images per language family with explicit layer contracts and TTL; (2) Add buildcache hit metrics and a small dashboard surfaced in Console for infra team; (3) Refresh and lock lint/toolchain versions in dedicated builder images; (4) Pilot a remote CAS-backed cache-proxy for heavy artifacts. Excludes full migration to alternative CI engine — that is tracked separately.
tasks: Audit top-200 CI jobs to identify largest layer churn (owner: Miguel) — due 2025-06-09
Prototype minimal Python/Node/Go base images with distroless slim + pinned OS packages (owner: Saira) — due 2025-06-18
Add transparent cache hit/miss metrics to buildkite hooks and push to prometheus (owner: Kofi) — due 2025-06-15
Implement a small Grafana dashboard and burn rate alert for buildcache efficiency (owner: Kofi) — due 2025-06-22
Consolidate linter/toolchain versions into 'ci-builder' image and run canary against 50 CI pipelines (owner: Priya) — due 2025-06-25
Proof-of-concept remote CAS-backed cache-proxy and validate artifact retrieval latency (owner: Miguel) — due 2025-06-30
Docs: update CONTRIBUTING.md with new cache semantics and how to add cacheable artifacts (owner: Saira) — due 2025-07-02
Rollout plan and rollback playbook for base image swap (owner: Miguel) — due 2025-07-04
acceptance_criteria: Average CI wall time for audited jobs reduced by >= 20% compared to 2025-05 baseline
CI builder images reduced combined layer count by at least 30% (measured via docker history) and total compressed size reduced by >= 35%
Cache hit rate for instrumented pipelines >= 88% after warmup across 2 weeks
No regressions in lint results across canary pipelines; CI flakiness rate for those pipelines < 1%
Prometheus metrics emitted: buildcache_hit_total, buildcache_miss_total, remote_cas_get_latency_seconds with Grafana dashboard linked
Runbook created and rollback tested for swapping base images in production pipelines
notes: Trade-offs: We intentionally keep the base image footprint minimal but not zero-dependency; some teams will need small per-repo layers for native deps (e.g., libsndfile). Those will be documented as 'non-shared' layers.
We chose a CAS-backed cache-proxy POC rather than full CAS migration to limit blast radius and allow gradual adoption.
Lint/toolchain lock: prefer semver windows + scheduled quarterly upgrades rather than tracking latest patch in CI to reduce churn.
We will not change the primary CI runner engine during this ticket; cross-team migration to a new runner is a follow-up project.
Security: pinned packages will be scanned by dependency scanner pipeline; any critical CVEs must be triaged before rollout.
updates: 2025-06-05: Initial audit completed — top 120 jobs cover 92% of CI minutes. Identified 5 repos responsible for >40% of layer churn due to large per-repo base modifications.
2025-06-07: Decision meeting with Platform and DX teams — agreed to ship three language-family base images and offer migration docs and a compatibility shim for repos that need extra tooling.
2025-06-09: Miguel pushed ENG-128275 (image-profiles) and ENG-128276 (metrics-hook) as child tickets. Miguel started canary on 12 low-risk pipelines.
2025-06-11: First metrics emitted to prometheus from buildkite hook. Initial cache hit rate on canary ~72% (still warming). Observed remote CAS GET p50 ~45ms in POC environment.

2025-06-10: Blocker: one internal repo depends on glibc 2.28 which conflicts with distroless base. Mitigation: add 'compat' layer and prioritize owners to refactor native deps (tracked in ENG-128279).
